headline: Improving execution and expanding capabilities to drive growth

highlights: We believe execution across LCA Tejas, helicopters, engines and other manufacturing programmes should support growth as company is entering a stronger execution phase.

On the Tejas Mk1A programme, HAL has prepared 27 aircraft airframes, while GE engine supplies have improved to 14 units (GE targets to deliver 28 by FY27E), with management aiming to deliver 10 jets by Mar-27 and 24+ jets annually post engines supply stabilisation.
Further, GE has been placed an order for 113 additional F404 engines for the second batch of 97 Tejas Mk1A aircraft, with deliveries scheduled in 2027-32.
These initiatives are expected to strengthen HAL’s manufacturing capabilities and support its long-term growth.
valuation: On the Tejas Mk1A programme, HAL has prepared 27 aircraft airframes, while GE engine supplies have improved to 14 units (GE targets to deliver 28 by FY27E), with management aiming to deliver 10 jets by Mar-27 and 24+ jets annually post engines supply stabilisation.

HAL is increasing annual production capacity for AL-31FP engines from 30 to 50 units with an investment of ₹335 crore and is setting up a second Shakti engine production line with an investment of ₹218 crore, targeting capacity of up to 100 engines annually by FY29.
Rating and Target Price : • We believe that HAL is strongly placed to benefit from pick-up in execution of existing strong order backlog and robust pipeline.
